title: Scheduled launch gating checklist and cutover ownership map for runtime/console/api
creator: Liam Chen
description: Objective: Create a single, actionable gating checklist and a cutover ownership map to coordinate a staggered launch across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. Deliverables: 1) A bullet-proof gating checklist for pre-canary, canary, staged-production, and full-cutover phases; 2) Ownership map (primary + backup) covering SRE, Runtime Eng, Console Eng, API Platform, Product, and Solutions; 3) Traffic-shift runbook with explicit timeboxes, rollback criteria, and automated safety gates; 4) Reserved capacity and escalation lanes for Dedicated customers; 5) Post-cutover validation matrix and metrics dashboard links. Scope excludes per-customer migration plans (handled by Customer Success).
acceptance_criteria: A single gating checklist published in Confluence and linked from release calendar
Owners assigned (primary + backup) for every gating item and cutover step
Automated metric checks wired into Canary pipeline for latency, error-rate, and token-cost regression
Traffic-shift runbook with step-by-step commands and exact traffic percentages (0->5->25->75->100) and windows defined
Rollback criteria documented and tested in a dry-run with a representative canary during staging week
Reserved GPU capacity slots and autoscaling guardrails confirmed with CloudOps for dedicated tenants
Post-mortem template and on-call rotation for first 72 hours post-cutover agreed
decisions: Use latency (p50/p95) and error-rate thresholds as primary automated gates; token-cost regressions will be monitored but not block-cutover under small (<5%) variance
Canary progression percentages will be 5%, 25%, 75%, 100% with minimum 30-minute steady-state checks unless explicit quick-advance is approved by SRE lead
All console-facing schema changes will use deferred migration flags to avoid coordinate-time coupling with backend rollout
Dedicated customers requiring reserved capacity will be served from a separate autoscaling pool to avoid noisy-neighbor risk
